note: blind on the diff at xhigh, read-only sandbox, no brief and no narrative. Its first finding is the one that mattered: a report holding only the reader's own entry returned RECONCILED, so zero peers masqueraded as fleet agreement — the disease the organ exists to detect, inside the organ. It also caught the absolute remote path (M5 /Users/balizero vs Pro /Users/nuzantara), the close marker recognised mid-line so prose quoting a tag ended the block early, and the parity test that asserted a SYMBOL NAME any reimplementation passes.

second cross-family seat on the same blind diff. It is the one that killed the DESIGN rather than a line: a single shared report is rewritten whole by every publisher, so A pushes {A} to B, C pushes {C} to B and A is simply gone — no lock, no re-merge on receipt, and the freshness stamps cannot tell an ERASED peer from a quiet one. Replaced with one fragment per machine. It also caught the clock-skew immortality (a future stamp never ages out), the scp with no BatchMode that wedges the publisher forever on a peer without key auth, and the over-match twin in the loop regex I had widened hours earlier.

verdict: 2 under-matches, both REPRODUCED on disk before being touched
note: A third cross-family read of the merged diff, after the two blind refuters had already signed off. Both findings are in the parser and both are silent: (1) the CANON: keyword is case-sensitive, so <!-- canon:x --> parsed to ZERO blocks and was not even flagged malformed; (2) no fence-awareness, so a <!-- CANON:id --> shown inside a fenced code block became a live comparable block. The second is the SAME class as L10-PR1 finding #2 earlier in this wave, which makes it a pattern rather than a slip. Reproduced this turn: an empty dict for the mis-cased pair, and a one-key dict keyed `example` for the fenced pair. The digest is not quoted — it is a sha256 prefix of fixture text and reads to detect-secrets as a high-entropy hex string, a real CI failure to buy for sixteen decorative characters (measured: it cost one).
